summary: Meta’s Context Language Models let models natively manage their own context.
why: The paper offers a new context-management approach worth testing in agent workflows.

summary: Context Language Models edit their live context as a file; reported gains include higher task accuracy and lower compute.
why: Letting agents rewrite working context could improve long tasks while reducing compute, with caching tradeoffs to manage.

summary: Flags a product policy that allows unlimited human use but caps agent use.
why: Agent-specific usage caps can affect the cost and reliability of your agent workflows.

summary: Build a model-agnostic harness so frequent model swaps don’t break your workflows.
why: A stable harness lets you test new models without repeatedly rebuilding your agent setup.

summary: Announces a DevDay stream covering connected workflows, sandboxes, physical AI and agent loops.
why: The agent-loop and sandbox sessions may offer ideas or demos applicable to your tooling.

summary: Teases using agent swarms to port software between technologies, with a claimed cost around $10.
why: The linked experiment may offer a concrete example of swarm-based code migration and its cost.

summary: Teases a GeoGuessr-style game where open AI models compete at identifying locations.
why: Could provide an engaging way to compare model capabilities, though no evaluation details are shared yet.

summary: Argues companies will hire automation engineers to embed with teams and build agents around their actual workflows.
why: The embedded-team model is a practical pattern for finding useful agent work beyond generic automation.

summary: Choose evaluators by weighing the cost of code-based checks against LLM judges; don't automate every failure mode by default.
why: Cost-aware eval selection helps you spend effort where automated checks are worth maintaining.

summary: A podcast guest reportedly said OpenAI's Decision API uses GPT-6 Luna with an added decision head.
why: The claimed architecture could offer a useful clue about building decision-focused model interfaces.

summary: Qodo 3.0 groups related cross-repo PRs into scored work packages and creates a shared review brief.
why: Helps reviewers prioritize and assess an agent's connected PRs together, rather than in isolation.

summary: Barclays is expanding its Anthropic partnership to deploy secure Claude systems across global operations.
why: Offers a real-world example of a regulated enterprise scaling Claude, though few implementation details are given.

summary: Explores how AI systems self-organize to complete tasks and what that implies for agent projects like Muse and Dots.
why: A useful mental model for designing agent systems that coordinate around tasks.

summary: Praises an AI-assisted editor that dims suggested removals instead of showing replacement text, and notes its workflow is visible in the UI.
why: The dimmed-removal pattern is a transferable way to make AI edits easier to review.

summary: Argues that model quality claims are hard to compare when token budgets, codebases, languages, teams, and requirements differ.
why: A reminder to evaluate models in your own workflow rather than generalize from mismatched experiences.

summary: Amp understood a Chinese bug report, fixed the issue, and drafted a reply in Chinese without the developer noticing the language switch.
why: A useful example of an agent handling a multilingual coding-and-communication workflow end to end.

summary: Shares a review of Claude’s new Auto Evals plugin and asks users to compare experiences.
why: The review may offer practical lessons for evaluating Claude-based agent workflows.
